0.label: head_face_oju_opon
0.description: A large face at the top of the tray's rim: heavy-lidded eyes, broad nose, full lips, three vertical cheek marks on each side, a crest of short strokes above, framed by hatched bars.
0.iconography: The ojú ọpọ́n, conventionally Ẹ̀ṣù, which the diviner orients the tray by. The cheek marks are ilà facial marks, which in Yoruba practice identify lineage or town.

1.label: kneeling_rifleman
1.description: A kneeling man in a peaked cap holding a long gun upright, its stock on the ground, in the rim compartment left of the head.
1.iconography: A rifleman — the same figure as on the tray EBA-Div_00302 (#1, human-annotated). A guard, or the danger a client asks about, in the war years of Modakeke.

2.label: sacrificial_fowl
2.description: A bird with a fan-grooved wing and a small head pointing down, in the left rim compartment below the rifleman.
2.iconography: The sacrificial fowl of Ifá, carved almost exactly as on EBA-Div_00302 (#2) — a strong sign of one workshop.

3.label: foot_face_inverted
3.description: A second face at the foot of the rim, carved upside down relative to the photograph so that it too looks into the centre; lidded eyes, nose and banded forehead.
3.iconography: A second ojú ọpọ́n at the opposite point, as on EBA-Div_00302 (#3/#7): two faces on one axis.

4.label: coupling_pair
4.description: Two figures lying together in the upper-left rim compartment, one over the other, legs entwined.
4.iconography: Sex and marriage as a matter brought to Ifá — the theme of the couples on EBA-Div_00302.

5.label: struggle_or_coupling_scene
5.description: In the lower-right compartment, a figure with a raised fist tumbling over a second, bearded head.
5.iconography: Either a fight or a coupling; the raised fist suggests conflict — a quarrel or violence put before the diviner.

6.label: mother_nursing_child
6.description: A seated figure holding a smaller round-headed figure to its chest, in the upper-right compartment.
6.iconography: A mother nursing a child (or an embracing couple): the hoped-for outcome of the fertility consultations shown elsewhere on the rim.

7.label: reclining_couple_lower_left
7.description: Two figures lying together in the lower-left rim compartment, one with its arm thrown across the other, heads side by side near the foot face.
7.iconography: A second coupling pair, matching #4 across the tray: union and children, the most common request put to Ifá.

8.label: crouching_rifleman_with_long_gun
8.description: In the upper-right compartment beside the head face, a man in a peaked cap crouches over a long gun held across his body, its butt resting on the ground line.
8.iconography: A second armed man, answering the kneeling rifleman (#1) on the other side of the face: guns flank Ẹ̀ṣù at the head of the tray, as they flank daily life in a war town.

9.label: reclining_figure_under_long_curved_object
9.description: In the lower-right compartment, a figure lying on its back with a hand raised to its face, beneath a long curved bar that runs the width of the compartment.
9.iconography: The bar may be a bow or a gun lying over a fallen or resting man. If fallen, the tray's rim moves from armed men at the head to a casualty at the foot.

panel.title: Modakeke Ifá tray: faces, rifleman, fowl, couples and a nursing mother
panel.summary: A round Ifá tray from Modakeke with a worn central field, a crack across it, and a rim carved with two faces on one axis, two riflemen, a fowl, coupling pairs, a nursing figure and a figure lying under a long curved bar.

register_readings.reading: The axis: a face at the head and an inverted face at the foot, both looking inward.
Left side of the rim: a couple, a kneeling rifleman, the sacrificial fowl, and a second couple near the foot.
Right side: a crouching rifleman beside the head, a nursing figure, a struggle or coupling, and a figure lying under a long curved bar near the foot.

panel.composition: A ring divided into about ten compartments around a used, empty centre, fixed by two faces on one diameter.
panel.narrative: The rim lays out a client's world as a diviner would meet it: desire and marriage, birth, conflict, the rifle, and the fowl to be sacrificed, with Ẹ̀ṣù's faces at head and foot. It almost repeats the tray EBA-Div_00302 motif for motif — same fowl, same rifleman, same couples, same lidded faces — so the two trays very probably come from one Modakeke workshop. For a town founded by war refugees and at war for decades, the rifle on a divining tray is history as much as symbol.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral-to-weak for 'chronicle' (a world, not a sequence); the rifle dates it to the war era. Not numerical.
cross_panel_links: Near-twin of EBA-Div_00302 — probably the same carver or workshop.
Faces with ilà marks link to FoA_04-5583 and FoA_04-5588.
The rifleman links to the Ado-Ekiti door EBA-Div_00303.
uncertainties: Several compartments are not boxed, so the programme is incomplete.
#5 could be a fight or a coupling.
